battle.name: 張起緒起義
battle.theater: 淮南江都廣陵沿淮一線
battle.brief: 大業十一年(615)七月，淮南人張起緒舉兵為盜，眾至三萬，郡兵不能制；同月隋煬帝北巡塞外，八月被突厥困於雁門，淮南的急報與北方的急報同時擺上案頭。卡面羅馬方陣盾未隨軍而至：中國軍中無此制式，叛軍靠漁具柴斧與粗弓，官軍仍是楯結陣、槊弩與札甲的郡兵。

kit.name: 羅馬方陣盾
kit.history: 凸面的長方盾。羅馬的防線靠盾緣咬住盾緣，不是靠盾牌多厚。

countries: 大業十一年(615)七月發生在淮南的這場起義，交戰的兩方是隋朝郡兵與淮南地方聚眾組成的武裝。這不是國家對國家的戰爭，而是一個王朝的基層兵制與一群靠劫掠維生的烏合之眾在同一片州郡裡面對撞。叛方的首領是張起緒，籍貫淮南，《隋書》稱他「舉兵為盜，眾至三萬」；這支部眾的來源多半是淮南各縣的逃戶、流民，以及被抽調而逃亡的丁役，其中也混著在江淮漕運上做慣了船工的漁戶與腳夫。他們沒有固定編制，沒有號令系統，也沒有留下可供核對的兵籍，軍令、糧秣與撤退都靠首領一人的號召維持。官方在淮南的力量由兩套人馬組成：一是江都、廣陵、山陽、海陵等郡的郡兵與縣卒，這些兵大體是鄉兵骨幹加臨時召募，裝備自備、訓練鬆散，遇大股強敵往往各自散歸田里；二是從關中與北方調來的中央兵，由行軍總管一級的將領節制，兵精甲利而數量有限，一旦離開中央便難以補充。淮南在隋朝的地位極其特殊：它既是運河的南端、江都的所在，是全國漕糧的出海口，又緊貼著已經被抽空了丁役的北方戰場。因此隋廷對這一區的控制，一半靠郡兵，一半靠漕運的暢通。第三方也始終在場：北方有正在打仗的高句麗與趁火打劫的突厥，江南的餘杭、會稽一帶有劉元進那樣的山澤武裝，淮南夾在這幾股力量之間，朝廷既不敢把主力全部押在江淮，也無法把淮南完全放著不管。
countriesEn: The rising that broke out in Huainan in the seventh month of the eleventh year of Daye (615) was fought between the commandery troops of the Sui and an armed multitude assembled from the local population of that region. It was not a war between states, but the collision of a dynasty's lowest-order military system with a rabble that lived on plunder, in the same commanderies. The leader of the rebels was Zhang Qixu, a native of Huainan, whom the History of the Sui describes as raising a bandit force of thirty thousand. The sources of this multitude were for the most part the runaway households, the vagrants and the conscripts who had fled from the levies of the commanderies of Huainan, with among them also the boatmen of the Jianghuai grain traffic and the fishermen and porters who worked the canals. They had no permanent establishment, no system of orders, and left behind no muster roll that can be checked; command, supply and withdrawal all rested on the personal call of the one leader. The official force in Huainan was made up of two different bodies. The first was the commandery soldiers and county levies of Jiangdu, Guangling, Shanyang, Hailing and the other commanderies; these were in substance a skeleton of militia soldiers supplemented by ad hoc recruitment, equipping themselves and trained badly, and when a serious enemy came they would commonly break up and return to their fields. The second was the central army sent down from Guanzhong and the north, controlled by commanders of the rank of director of the campaign forces, with good men and good armour but limited numbers, and hard to replace once they had left the centre. Huainan's position within the Sui was quite special: it was the southern end of the canal and the seat of Jiangdu, the mouth through which the empire's grain tax left the country, and at the same time it lay hard against a northern front that had already been drained of its labour. Sui control of that region therefore rested half on the commandery soldiers and half on the smooth running of the grain traffic. Third parties were present throughout as well: in the north there was Goguryeo, at war with the Sui, and the Turks, ready to pick off what they could; in the south, around Yuhang and Kuaiji, there were mountain bands of the kind represented by Liu Yuanjin. Huainan lay between these forces, and the court could neither commit its main strength to Jianghuai nor leave Huainan entirely to itself.
people: 史書為這場起義留下的唯一人名是張起緒，而且是作為籍貫加動作的標記留下來的：淮南人，舉兵為盜，眾至三萬。他的年齡、出身、原任的官職，以及這支部眾的編制，兩部史書都沒有交代；記錄呈現的是一個聚合了三萬人的地方首領形象，而不是一位有軍銜的將領，他與部眾之間靠什麼維繫，也沒有留下線索。同一時間在淮南活動的另一位首領是李子通，此人出身東海郡嶧縣的漁戶，大業十一年十月渡淮、自號楚王、寇江都，隨後在江淮經營數年，最終建吳國；把這兩人放在一起看，可以看出淮南那一年聚起的並不止一股武裝，而且彼此之間存在競爭。隋廷方面的關鍵人物是煬帝本人：七月淮南的急報送到時，他正在北上巡塞的途中；八月乙丑他抵達雁門即被突厥始畢可汗率數十萬騎包圍，城中兵民十五萬口、存糧只支二十日、雁門四十一城被突厥克去三十九，圍城數十日，直到天下募兵的援軍到來才解圍而還。淮南的事只能在這樣的背景下處理，朝廷既抽不出兵，也不敢把主力從北方戰線上拉走。真正被派往江南平亂的是樊子蓋，他帶著關中兵南下，戰果卻是「經年不能剋」，大業十二年七月病卒於軍中，他一死，關中方向的追討之勢隨之渙散。地方上還有李淵、竇建德、杜伏威這些後來在隋末各自成事的人：杜伏威自淮南起兵，李淵在太原、竇建德在河北，他們都看見了同一件事——隋朝的號令出了州郡就變成空話，而在一個號令失效的國家裡，先站出來的人就是秩序的制作者。
peopleEn: The only personal name the historical records preserve for this rising is that of Zhang Qixu, and it is preserved as a tag of origin plus an action: a native of Huainan, who raised a bandit force of thirty thousand. His age, his background, the office he had held and the organisation of his followers are all absent from both histories; what the record presents is the image of a local leader who had gathered thirty thousand men, not that of a commander with a rank, and nothing is left about what held him and his men together. A second leader active in Huainan at the same time was Li Zitong, the son of a fishing household in the Yi county of Donghai commandery; in the tenth month of the eleventh year of Daye he crossed the Huai, proclaimed himself King of Chu and struck at Jiangdu, and went on to work the Jianghuai for several years until he founded the state of Wu. Set the two of them side by side and it is clear that more than one armed body had formed in Huainan that year, and that they competed with one another. The decisive figure on the Sui side was the Emperor Yang himself. When the alarm from Huainan reached the court in the seventh month he was on his way north on a tour of the frontier; on the yichou day of the eighth month he reached Yanmen and was at once surrounded by the tens of thousands of horsemen of the Turkic kaghan Jiebi. There were one hundred and fifty thousand soldiers and civilians in the city, the grain would have held for twenty days only, and the Turks took thirty-nine of the forty-one cities of Yanmen; the siege lasted a number of tens of days, and it was only the levies raised throughout the empire that relieved it and carried him away. The affair in Huainan had to be handled against that background: the court could not draw troops away, and did not dare move its main strength off the northern front. The man actually sent south to suppress the disorder was Fan Zigai, who came down with the troops of Guanzhong and whose result was that he could not take the rebels in a year; in the seventh month of the twelfth year of Daye he died of illness in the field, and with him the momentum of the pursuit from Guanzhong dissolved. On the local side there were the men who would each make a state of themselves in the late Sui: Du Fuwei rose in Huainan, Li Yuan sat at Taiyuan and Dou Jiande in Hebei. All of them had seen the same thing — that the orders of the Sui became empty words once they crossed the borders of a commandery, and that in a state whose orders had failed, whoever stood up first became the maker of the new order.
kits: 卡面這面羅馬方陣盾(scutum)不在這場起義的裝備表裡。它是共和末期至帝國時期羅馬步兵的主力盾：木條拼成的長方體略作弧形，外面蒙皮，正面留有兩個鐵乳突，寬約一公尺、高約七、八十公分。它的價值不在於厚薄，而在於盾緣可以相互咬合，讓一列步兵把箭雨與投槍的衝力分擔掉，同時遮住從膝到肩的身體。時間上它比大業十一年早七百多年，地理上在歐亞的另一端，淮南的碼頭與泥岸上不可能出現這種盾牌。它能提供的只是一條比較用的尺子：用制式大盾結成的密集線，與沒有制式大盾的臨時隊伍，在承受衝擊時完全是兩回事。淮南這邊實際使用的是中國式的防具與兵器。官方的郡兵按《隋書》兵式志所載的制度配裝：木胎蒙漆皮或牛皮的楯，內裡綴竹木條以抗箭；鎧甲以札甲為主，另有披掛與護具；近戰是直刃的橫刀與環首刀、長柄的槊與戈；遠射是角弓、漆弓與弩，弩以木臂竹機為多；大盾與手盾同樣常見於隊列之中。叛軍這邊的裝備史書完全沒有記載，只能拿同年淮南另一支武裝作參照：他們多半只有漁叉、柴斧、短刀與粗弓，箭鏃用石用鐵都不定，靠的是水網中的舟船而不是步戰；杜伏威在淮南的隊伍要到後來才按「設軍令、行賞罰、小隊作戰」的方式整頓過，說明在張起緒這個層級上，武裝仍然是散兵式的，沒有制度。在這條地區，決定勝負的往往不是兵器而是船：邗溝、淮水與江南水網把淮南切成一片片被水隔開的陸塊，誰控制船，誰就控制得到糧、逃得掉、打得著。攻城用的撞車、雲梯與飛石車掌握在中央調來的兵手上，郡兵與叛軍都沒有；反過來說，叛軍同樣沒有能力攻破一座像樣的郡城，這正是「聚眾為盜」與「舉兵攻城」之間的差別。
kitsEn: The Roman scutum on the card does not belong in the equipment table of this rising. It was the standard shield of Roman infantry from the late Republic into the Empire: a rectangle of joined wooden staves, slightly curved, covered with hide, with two iron bosses on the face, about a metre wide and seventy or eighty centimetres high. Its value lay not in thickness but in the fact that the rims could interlock, so that a rank of infantry could share out the shock of arrows and javelins while covering the body from knee to shoulder. In time it preceded the eleventh year of Daye by more than seven centuries, and in place it stood on the far side of Eurasia; nothing of the kind could have appeared on the wharves and mud banks of Huainan. What it offers is a ruler for comparison: a dense line formed of standard large shields, and a hastily raised body without them, are two entirely different things when a charge lands on them. The equipment actually used in Huainan was of the Chinese sort. The official commandery soldiers were equipped according to the regulations recorded in the treatises on military matters in the History of the Sui: shields of wood covered with lacquered hide or rawhide, strengthened inside with bamboo and wooden strips against arrows; armour of the scaled kind, together with surcoats and limb guards; for close fighting, straight-edged sabres and ring-pommel swords, and long-handled spears and ge; for shooting at range, bows of horn and lacquered wood, and crossbows, most of them with wooden arms and bamboo locks; large shields and small hand shields were equally common in the ranks. The rebels' equipment is simply not recorded, and one can only use the other armed body in Huainan that same year as a reference: they had for the most part fish forks, woodcutters' axes, short knives and coarse bows, arrowheads of stone or of iron as the case might be, and they relied on boats in the water network rather than on fighting on foot. The band Du Fuwei raised in Huainan was only reorganised later along the lines of a declared military law, rewards and punishments, and fighting in small units, which shows that at Zhang Qixu's level the armament was still that of scattered bands without institutions. In this region what usually decided the outcome was not the weapon but the boat: the Hangou, the Huai and the water network of the south cut Huainan into stretches of land separated by water, and whoever controlled the boats controlled the grain, the means of escape and the means of striking. The battering ram, the scaling ladder and the stone-thrower were in the hands of the troops brought down from the centre; neither the commandery soldiers nor the rebels had them. In the other direction, the rebels were equally unable to break a properly fortified commandery city, and that is exactly the difference between a mob that gathers and a rising that takes a city.
tactics: 淮南的作戰方式，首先受地形支配。這一帶河湖縱橫、蘆蕩千里，村落與城鎮多隔水相望，道路是堤埂而不是車道，因此大軍作戰、攻城器械與糧車都受極大限制。三萬人的聚眾要在這樣的地界裡行動，靠的是分散與轉移，而不是列陣。張起緒這支部眾起兵之後最合理的部署是據城、據鄉里為據點，平日分隊劫掠、得食即散，官軍一到便退入水網或山寨，這是隋末江淮武裝的共同做法：李子通用船戶出身，能在白沙河道夜航避開郡兵巡哨；杜伏威的隊伍在江淮打了七年游擊，也是同一套邏輯——不打官軍主力，只欺負分遣出城的小股部隊，打完即退，並用火攻與船隊切斷運河上的糧道。對隋廷而言，平叛的辦法有兩種：一是靠郡兵與縣卒在本地逐城清剿，優點是熟悉水道、隨時可調，缺點是裝備差、訓練鬆，遇強即散；二是把關中兵與北方精兵調下來，以中央軍的裝備與訓練攻破每一處據點，缺點是遠、耗、而且一敗就全盤崩。七月之後朝廷用的正是第二種辦法，樊子蓋與關中兵南下，平叛的效果是「經年不能剋」。要理解這一點，還得看同時發生的雁門之戰：北方精騎被突厥困在雁門，淮南的郡兵又不足以獨力討平三萬眾，隋朝在大業十一年裡同時缺人、缺馬、缺糧，戰線拉得越長，這種到處缺兵的狀況就越嚴重。張起緒部最後如何覆滅，兩部史書都沒有記下作戰過程，只能從淮南局勢此後的變化看出：十月李子通渡淮自號楚王，兩年之後杜伏威在淮南崛起，隋朝的號令在這片江淮再沒有一年真正落實過。
tacticsEn: The way fighting was done in Huainan was dictated first of all by the terrain. Rivers and lakes run everywhere, reed beds stretch to the horizon, villages and walled towns stand across water from one another, and the roads are levees rather than cart tracks, so that massed operations, siege engines and supply wagons were all severely restricted. A multitude of thirty thousand moving in such a country could only do so by dispersal and by shifting position, not by forming up in line. The most plausible deployment of Zhang Qixu's men after they rose was to hold towns and villages as bases, to raid in parties by day, to disperse as soon as they had eaten, and to fall back into the water network or into the hills whenever the government troops came; this was the common practice of the Jianghuai bands in the last years of the Sui. Li Zitong, the son of a boatman, could move at night through the Baisha channel to avoid the patrols of the commandery soldiers; Du Fuwei's band spent seven years in the Jianghuai fighting the same kind of war, never engaging the main body of the Sui army but only the small detachments sent out of the cities, breaking off after the stroke and using fire and boat parties to cut the grain route of the canal. For the court there were two ways to suppress such a rising. The first was to let the commandery and county soldiers clear the cities one by one, locally; the advantage was their familiarity with the waterways and their readiness to move at any time, the disadvantage was poor equipment, slack training, and a tendency to melt away when a real enemy appeared. The second was to bring down the troops of Guanzhong and the picked troops of the north and use the equipment and discipline of the central army to break every stronghold in turn; the disadvantage was distance, exhaustion, and the fact that a single defeat could bring the whole thing down. After the seventh month the court used the second method, and the outcome of Fan Zigai and the troops of Guanzhong coming south was that they could not take the rebels in a year. To understand that, one has to look at the siege of Yanmen happening at the same time: the picked cavalry of the north was shut up in Yanmen by the Turks, and the commandery soldiers of Huainan were not strong enough to defeat thirty thousand men by themselves. Throughout the eleventh year of Daye the Sui lacked men, horses and grain at once, and the longer the front became, the worse this want of troops everywhere became. How Zhang Qixu's band was finally destroyed is not recorded in either history; only the subsequent change in the situation of Huainan shows it: in the tenth month Li Zitong crossed the Huai and proclaimed himself King of Chu, and two years later Du Fuwei rose in Huainan, and after that the orders of the Sui were never once truly carried out in this Jianghuai.
data: 可核對的數字分三類。第一類是本役自身的：起事繫於大業十一年(615)七月，《隋書·煬帝紀》只留下「淮南人張起緒舉兵為盜，眾至三萬」一句，沒有戰果、沒有斬首數、沒有平定日期；「三萬」是史家對地方聚眾的概數，多半含裹挾的民眾與流民，不宜當作野戰兵解讀，也沒有留下編制。與同年其他亂事可以對照的數字是：二月「賊帥楊仲緒率眾萬餘，攻北平」，同月滑公李景破斬之；同月上谷人王須拔反，自稱漫天王、國號燕，賊帥魏刁兒自稱歷山飛，眾各十餘萬；十月彭城人魏騏驎聚眾萬餘為盜、寇魯郡，賊帥盧明月聚眾十餘萬寇陳汝間，東海賊帥李子通渡淮自號楚王；十二月譙郡人朱粲擁眾數十萬寇荊襄、僭稱楚帝建元昌達。第二類是同年的背景量級：八月乙丑隋煬帝巡北塞，戊午突厥始畢可汗率騎數十萬至雁門，城中兵民十五萬口、食僅可支二旬，突厥克雁門四十一城之三十九，直到九月甲辰解圍。《資治通鑑》記大業八年第一次征高句麗發兵百十三萬五千八百人，渡河者三十萬五千，士卒死者十之八九，歸國者不過二三千；大業末年《隋書·地理志》所記全州郡戶八百九十餘萬、丁四百六十餘萬，經三征高句麗與關中大旱，只存一半上下。第三類是地理與里程，可以核算：淮南郡縣密集，江都(今江蘇揚州)經邗溝北至山陽(今淮安)約一百二十里，再由淮入汴、經泗、宿、宋、汴抵洛陽，全程以千餘里計；江淮水道交錯，隋朝漕運一條線斷在何處，淮南的亂事就會在哪裡變成災難。張起緒部的確切人數、所部編制、攻城與野戰的損失，兩部史書一概無數可對，不應補造。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into three classes. The first concerns the rising itself. It is dated to the seventh month of the eleventh year of Daye (615), and the History of the Sui in the annals of Emperor Yang preserves a single sentence: a native of Huainan, Zhang Qixu, raised a bandit force, and the multitude reached thirty thousand. There is no record of results, no number of the slain, and no date of suppression. Thirty thousand is the historian's summary figure for a local multitude and must have included a good deal of coerced common people and vagrants; it should not be read as a field strength, and no establishment is recorded. The figures that can be set against it from the same year are these: in the second month the bandit leader Yang Zhongyi gathered more than ten thousand and attacked Beiping, and the Duke of Hua Li Jing cut him down in the same month; in that same month a man of Shanggu named Wang Xuba rebelled, styling himself King of Man and founding the state of Yan, while the bandit leader Wei Diao'er styled himself Lord of Lishan, each with more than a hundred thousand men; in the tenth month Wei Qilin of Pengcheng raised more than ten thousand as bandits and raided Lu commandery, the bandit leader Lu Mingyue gathered over a hundred thousand and raided the region of Chen and Ru, and the bandit leader of Donghai, Li Zitong, crossed the Huai and proclaimed himself King of Chu; in the twelfth month Zhu Can of Qiao commandery, with several tens of thousands, raided Jing and Xiang and usurped the title Son of Chu with the era name Changda. The second class is the scale of the background in the same year: on the yichou day of the eighth month the Emperor Yang went on a tour of the northern frontier, and on the wuwu day the Turkic kaghan Jiebi brought tens of thousands of horsemen to Yanmen, where there were one hundred and fifty thousand soldiers and civilians, grain sufficient for only twenty days, and of the forty-one cities of Yanmen the Turks took thirty-nine; the siege was not lifted until the jiachen day of the ninth month. The Comprehensive Mirror records that in the eighth year of Daye, for the first campaign against Goguryeo, the Sui mustered one million one hundred and thirty-five thousand eight hundred men, of whom three hundred and five thousand crossed the river, and that of the soldiers nine in ten died, so that no more than two or three thousand returned. The Geography treatise of the History of the Sui records, at the height of the dynasty, more than eight million nine hundred thousand households and more than four million six hundred thousand adult males throughout the commanderies and counties; after the three campaigns against Goguryeo and the great drought in Guanzhong, only about half of that remained. The third class is geography and mileage, which can be checked. The commanderies of Huainan were closely packed: from Jiangdu, present-day Yangzhou in Jiangsu, north along the Hangou to Shanyang, present-day Huai'an, is about one hundred and twenty li, and from there the route ran into the Bian river and on through Si, Su, Song and Bian to Luoyang, a journey of more than a thousand li. With the waterways of the Jianghuai crossing one another in every direction, wherever the Sui grain traffic was broken, a disturbance in Huainan became a disaster. The exact number of Zhang Qixu's men, the organisation of his force, and the losses on both sides in field and siege alike are simply not in either history, and they should not be invented.
cause: 淮南會出這樣一支三萬人的隊伍，原因是四層。第一層是兵制：隋朝的府兵與郡兵大體建立在「民年二十為兵、役訖歸田」的鄉兵骨幹之上，兵歸府、番役與訓練相間，太平時兵在田而府有籍；到了大業年間，三征高句麗把能調的精壯都抽去了北邊，留在淮南的只剩下被攤薄得近乎空殼的守備，郡兵早已名存實亡。郡兵一空，任何一個有號召力的人聚起數千上萬人，就是當地不可忽略的力量。第二層是徭役與漕運：淮南是全國產米產鹽之地，卻也是運河北上的出海口，隋朝的軍糧有一半靠它；丁役被大批抽去遼東與北方戰線，江淮的農民在田間與漕船之間兩頭受擾，逃亡與流亡成了常態，盜匪的兵源正是這些逃戶與流民。第三層是政治：隋朝末年朝廷對地方的訊息管道是壞的，御史與政事堂把各地的告變表狀一律減損，煬帝因此對真實的亂局規模幾乎一無所知；淮南的叛軍在七月能拉起三萬人，恰恰說明地方社會的抵抗早已成形，而中央還在按老皇上的成例辦事。第四層是權力真空：淮南一帶沒有足以服眾的大人物站出來組織，這使得起義只能停留在「聚眾為盜」的層次——有眾而無號令，有破壞力而無政治目標；這樣的起義往往短暫而殘酷，因為它既不能給部眾出路，也不能給地方真正的秩序，只會把糧、兵、器械一起燒掉，等於替後來收拾局面的人騰地方。
causeEn: A force of thirty thousand could form in Huainan for four reasons, layered one on another. The first is the military system. The Sui commandery soldiers and garrison levies rested in substance on a militia skeleton of the kind that took a man into service at twenty and returned him to his field when his turn was done, with the soldiers enrolled in the bureaux and turns of service and drilling mixed together; in time of peace the men stayed in the fields and the registers were kept. By the years of Daye, three campaigns against Goguryeo had drawn away to the north every able man who could be found, and what remained in Huainan was a garrison thinned to a shell, the commandery soldiers existing in name only. Once that army was hollow, any man with the gift of gathering people could raise thousands or tens of thousands and become a force the local authorities could not ignore. The second is labour and transport. Huainan was the country that grew the empire's rice and salt, and it was also the mouth through which the Sui grain tax went north; half the army's provisions came from it. The conscripts were drawn away in large numbers to Liaodong and to the northern fronts, and the peasantry of the Yangzi and Huai were harried from both sides, between the fields and the grain boats, and flight and vagrancy became the normal condition. The manpower of the bandits was precisely these runaway households and vagrants. The third is politics. The channel by which the late Sui court heard about the localities was broken: the censors and the secretariat routinely reduced and trimmed the reports of disturbances from every region, so that the Emperor Yang knew almost nothing of the true scale of the disorder. That a rebellion in Huainan could raise thirty thousand men by the seventh month is itself the proof that resistance had long taken shape in the local society, while the centre was still going through the motions of the old imperial routine. The fourth is the vacuum of authority. In the Huainan region no figure of sufficient standing emerged to organise anything, and that is why the rising could only remain what the annals call a gathering of bandits: a multitude without orders, destructive force without a political aim. Such risings tend to be short and brutal, because they can offer their followers neither a livelihood nor any real order for the district; they burn the grain, the weapons and the tools, and in doing so clear the ground for whoever is to come next and take charge.
impact: 這場起義本身的記錄很短，餘波卻很長。第一，淮南的治安問題從此成為隋朝無法解決的常態：七月淮南人起兵、十月李子通渡淮自號楚王、兩年後杜伏威在淮南崛起，三年之內同一片水網上出了三股武裝，隋朝的郡兵一次也沒有真正贏過，江淮在名義上仍是隋朝的一州一郡，實際上已經不受控制。第二，漕運這條線暴露了脆弱：只要淮南有一支能控制船隻的武裝，隋朝的軍糧就多一段風險，而北方正在打仗的消耗從不停止，斷一次漕運就等於在前線加一次饑荒。第三，制度的應對方式本身就是問題的證明：朝廷只能靠從關中與北方抽調精兵來打，樊子蓋帶著關中兵南下仍「經年不能剋」，大業十二年七月他一死，關中方向的追討之勢隨之渙散，等於宣告中央對江南的軍事能力只剩下一支隨時會耗盡的兵；同一套邏輯再往南寫一遍，就是617年宇文化及攻潼關、618年煬帝死於江都、隋朝崩潰的結局。第四，情報與言論的失真：虞世基把各地的告敗表狀減損上報，煬帝對前線的真實處境長期被蒙蔽，等到局勢無法收拾，處置的空間已經用盡。第五，這場起義給後世留下一份江淮亂局的樣本：它與同年的王須拔、魏騏驎、盧明月、朱粲一起，說明隋末的地方武裝可以憑「劫掠加流動」在半年內成軍，而它一旦佔住水網與運河，任何王朝都得用數倍的兵力與時間才能重新拿回去。唐朝在杜伏威歸降之後重整江淮的州縣與漕運，正是對這一段教訓的直接回應。
impactEn: The record of this rising is short, but the ripples of it are long. First, the security problem of Huainan became a permanent condition the Sui could not solve: a native of Huainan rose in the seventh month, Li Zitong crossed the Huai and proclaimed himself King of Chu in the tenth, and two years later Du Fuwei rose in Huainan; within three years three armed bodies had formed on the same stretch of water network, and not once did the Sui commandery soldiers actually win. Nominally Jianghuai remained a commandery and a county of the Sui; in practice it was no longer under control. Second, the grain route showed where it was vulnerable. If a single armed body in Huainan could control the boats, then the Sui army's food had one more exposed stage, while the consumption of the fighting in the north never stopped; every break in the grain traffic was one more famine added to the front. Third, the way the institutions answered is itself the proof of the problem. The court could only fight by drawing picked troops down from Guanzhong and the north, and Fan Zigai came south with the troops of Guanzhong and still could not take the rebels in a year; when he died of illness in the field in the seventh month of the twelfth year of Daye, the momentum of the pursuit from Guanzhong dissolved with him, which amounted to an announcement that the centre's military capacity for Jiangnan was down to a single force that would exhaust itself. Write the same logic out one stage further and it becomes Yuwen Huaji breaking through the Tong Pass in 617, the Emperor Yang dead at Jiangdu in 618, and the end of the Sui. Fourth, information and its reporting had failed: Yu Shiji trimmed the reports of defeat arriving from every region before submitting them, so that the Emperor Yang was long blinded to the real condition of the fronts, and by the time the situation could no longer be managed there was no room left to manage it with. Fifth, this rising left later generations a sample of disorder in the Jianghuai. Together with Wang Xuba, Wei Qilin, Lu Mingyue and Zhu Can of the same year, it shows that a local armed body in the late Sui could be raised to full size within half a year on nothing but plunder and movement, and that once such a body held the waterways and the canal, any dynasty would need several times the troops and a great deal of time to take the country back. The Tang, after Du Fuwei's submission, reorganised the commanderies and the grain traffic of the Jianghuai, and that was a direct answer to the lesson of these years.
result: 就這場起義本身而言，結果是記錄有限而結局不明。可以確定的是：大業十一年七月，淮南人張起緒舉兵為盜，眾至三萬，郡兵不能制止；同年八月，隋煬帝被突厥困在雁門，淮南的急報與北方的急報同時擺在御案之前，朝廷派出的關中兵由樊子蓋率領南下，經年不能剋，樊子蓋大業十二年七月病卒軍中。史書沒有記錄張起緒本人何時被平、被誰平、死在何處，他的名字此後再未出現；這份沉默本身就是結果的一部分：隋朝的編年在此處失去對江南的實際追蹤。可以從前後局勢推出的只有這一點：這支部眾並沒有改變淮南的最終歸屬——大業十一年十月李子通渡淮、自號楚王、寇江都，兩年後杜伏威在淮南起兵，到618年江都失守、隋朝覆亡，619年李子通克江都建吳國，622年杜伏威降唐，江淮最後歸入唐朝的版圖。也就是說，張起緒這支隊伍是隋末江淮崩解過程中的一段插曲：它用三萬人的規模證明了淮南的郡兵與漕運秩序已經無力自保，卻沒有能力建立任何替代品，最終被更大的武裝與更大的王朝一併收編。對後世而言，這場戰爭的意義更多在於它把隋末亂世的第一個關鍵問題擺到檯面上——兵不過是徵來的，糧不過是運來的，船不過是水網裡的船；當這三樣都失序，任何地方都可能在一夜之間變成戰場。
resultEn: As for this rising itself, the result is that the record is thin and the ending is unknown. What can be established is this: in the seventh month of the eleventh year of Daye, Zhang Qixu, a native of Huainan, raised a bandit force which reached thirty thousand, and the commandery soldiers could not stop it. In the eighth month the Emperor Yang was shut up in Yanmen by the Turks, and the alarm from Huainan and the alarm from the north lay on the imperial desk together; the troops of Guanzhong sent down under Fan Zigai could not take the rebels in a year, and Fan Zigai died of illness in the field in the seventh month of the twelfth year of Daye. Neither history records when Zhang Qixu was put down, by whom, or where he died, and his name never appears again; that silence is itself part of the result, for at this point the Sui annals lose all effective track of the south of the river. Only one thing can be inferred from the situation before and after: this band did not change where Huainan finally belonged. In the tenth month of the eleventh year of Daye Li Zitong crossed the Huai, proclaimed himself King of Chu and struck at Jiangdu; two years later Du Fuwei rose in Huainan; in 618 Jiangdu fell and the Sui was destroyed; in 619 Li Zitong took Jiangdu and founded the state of Wu; in 622 Du Fuwei submitted to the Tang, and the Jianghuai was finally folded into the empire of the Tang. Zhang Qixu's band was thus an episode in the dissolution of the Jianghuai in the last years of the Sui. It proved, with a strength of thirty thousand, that the commandery soldiers and the grain order of Huainan could no longer defend themselves, but it had the capacity to build no substitute of its own, and it was absorbed along with everything else by larger armed bodies and a larger dynasty. For later ages the meaning of this war lies less in the fighting than in the fact that it put the first essential question of the late Sui disorder on the table: soldiers are only conscripted, grain is only transported, and boats are only boats in a water network. Once all three of these lose their order, any district can become a battlefield overnight.
